content: Hiberix is a sterile, lyophilized powder that must be reconstituted at the time of use with the provided saline diluent for intramuscular injection. The vaccine contains the capsular polysaccharide of Haemophilus influenzae type b, which is a high molecular weight polymer known as polyribosyl-ribitol-phosphate. This polysaccharide is derived from the Haemophilus influenzae type b strain 20,752, which is cultivated in a synthetic medium. The medium undergoes heat inactivation and subsequent purification to ensure safety and efficacy. The vaccine also includes tetanus toxoid, which is produced from Clostridium tetani grown in a semi-synthetic medium. The tetanus toxin is detoxified using formaldehyde and then purified. The capsular polysaccharide is covalently linked to the tetanus toxoid, forming a conjugate. After the conjugate is purified, it is lyophilized in the presence of lactose, which acts as a stabilizer. The accompanying saline diluent contains 9% sodium chloride and is supplied in prefilled TIP-LOK syringes. The vaccine may contain up to 5 micrograms of residual formaldehyde as a result of the manufacturing process. Hiberix does not contain any preservatives. However, the tip caps of the prefilled syringes may contain natural rubber latex. Importantly, the rubber plungers of the prefilled syringes and the vial stoppers are latex-free.
